chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who is afflicted by janabah, while he has wounds or sores, or he fears for himself because of the cold, he said: “He does not perform ghusl and performs tayammum.”

key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.ٱلْبَرْدِ: cold that may cause harm or hardship
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if ghusl would cause harm because of wounds or cold?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one in a state of janabah who has wounds, sores, or fears harm from severe cold. In such a case, he should not perform ghusl but instead perform tayammum, showing the facilitation in the Shari'ah when water use is harmful.
